interpretation: Exploratory finite orientation/reflection checks and field radial diagnostics after external-library failure. No target decision/model or covariance is changed by this diagnostic.
findings: The archived field grids are identical to the official spatial STDPSF sampling. Oversampling4, gridorigin(50,50), native pixel-integrated response and free-flux normalization are internally consistent.
The independent cubic evaluator reproduces Photutils ImagePSF to floating-point precision and all four archived field-fit chi-squares to about1e-6 absolute.
The original orientation is best among all eight quarter-turn/reflection alternatives in every exposure; there is no evidence here for a transpose or detector-axis convention error.

Native retained pixels have a coherent radius-dependent mean mismatch with the fixed library, particularly10–23percent integrated excess at radius4–5nativepixels. Thousands of chi-square units originate beyond the masked saturated core.

These field data identify a failed mean instrumental response, not a valid gravitational test or an error-bar problem. Epoch/wavefront, charge spreading and spectral response are candidate causes; this diagnostic does not uniquely identify which physical instrumental contribution produces the mismatch.
scope_limit: One independently identified Gaia field star, BP-RP1.7092, is not a complete same-colour/spatial calibration for all quasar images. A learned mean-response correction would require a separately declared transfer/validation procedure before target application; covariance inflation is not such a correction.
